title: Subject-matter jurisdiction
summary: Subject-matter jurisdiction is a court’s authority to decide a category of dispute. Federal courts require an applicable grant of authority within the limits allowed by the Constitution.
notes: The parties cannot create missing subject-matter jurisdiction merely by agreeing to federal adjudication. Whether a particular legal requirement is actually jurisdictional requires interpretation; Lacks illustrates the importance of that classification.

sections.Meaning: Subject-matter jurisdiction is a court’s authority to decide a category of dispute. Federal courts require an applicable grant of authority within the limits allowed by the Constitution.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the statute authorizing the federal claim or action. The course emphasizes diversity, federal questions, supplemental jurisdiction, and removal. State the jurisdictional facts, distinguish them from facts proving liability, and check any statutory restrictions.
